title: Evaluation identifies the punctual ringed site with ordinary modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be the category with one object $*$ and only its identity morphism, equipped with the topology whose only covering sieve is the maximal sieve. For a commutative ring $R$, let $\underline R$ be the ring sheaf with value $R$. Evaluation at $*$ is an exact equivalence from sheaves of $\underline R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] to $R$-modules, with inverse the constant presheaf. It identifies sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] with ordinary tensor products. For a ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to S$, it intertwines sheaf extension and restriction of scalars with ordinary extension and restriction, including the unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Applying evaluation degreewise gives equivalences on cochain complexes, homotopy categories, and derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], commuting with localization and preserving quasi-isomorphisms and K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Thus the K-flat computation of derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on this site is the ordinary-module K-flat computation, respecting the extension-of-scalars unit.

source.place: Tag 00X9, section-topoi, paragraph following Definition 00XA (definition-topos): the punctual topos; module and tensor specialization of this identification

proof.text: Write $E_R(\mathcal M)=\mathcal M(*)$ and let $C_R(M)$ have value $M$ at $*$ and identity restriction. A matching family for the sole covering sieve consists of one section indexed by $\mathrm{id}_*$; its unique amalgamation is that section. Thus every presheaf is a sheaf. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the data of a module sheaf are precisely one $R$-module, and a morphism is precisely one $R$-linear map: the identity restriction is forced by the presheaf identity law. The maps $E_RC_R(M)\to M$ and $C_RE_R(\mathcal M)\to\mathcal M$ with component the identity are natural isomorphisms. Their triangle identities are identities at $*$. This constructs the asserted equivalence and its specified inverse.

source.place: Tag 00X9, section-topoi, punctual topos paragraph after definition-topos (00XA); explicit module specialization

proof.text: The equivalence just constructed is additive, since addition of module-sheaf morphisms is addition of their sole component. For a map $a:M\to N$, the presheaves with values $\ker a$ and $N/\operatorname{im}a$ are already sheaves by step 1. They have the kernel and cokernel universal properties because a factorization of a module-sheaf map is exactly a factorization of its sole component. This also agrees with the kernel/cokernel description in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Hence both $E_R$ and $C_R$ preserve kernels and cokernels and are exact. For any small family $(M_i)$ the sheaf with value $\bigoplus_iM_i$ is its coproduct, since maps from it are precisely families of maps from the $M_i$. Evaluation therefore also preserves all direct sums used below.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian, specialized using sites.tex Tag 00X9; direct universal-property verification

proof.text: By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the presheaf tensor product of $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N$ has sole value $\mathcal M(*)\otimes_R\mathcal N(*)$. It is a sheaf by step 1. The sheafification universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] identifies its sheafification with itself: the identity map has the same factorization property, so the two maps supplied by the universal properties are inverse. Consequently the tensor comparison sends each $m\otimes n$ to the same $m\otimes n$ at $*$. It is natural, and its associativity, symmetry and unit compatibilities hold on pure tensors (which generate the tensor products). Thus it is the ordinary tensor product, with its usual structure maps.

Let $\varphi:R\to S$. By [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], restriction changes the action at $*$ to $r\cdot n=\varphi(r)n$, leaving elements and maps unchanged. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and step 3, extension has sole value $M\otimes_RS$ and sends $a$ to $a\otimes1$. The extension/restriction adjunction is explicit here: $u:M\otimes_RS\to N$ corresponds to $m\mapsto u(m\otimes1)$; an $R$-linear $v:M\to N$ has inverse transpose $m\otimes s\mapsto s v(m)$, well defined by the balancing relation. Both composites are identities, and the formulas commute with maps of $M,N$. Taking $u$ to be the identity gives the unit $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. These formulas are identical for sheaves and modules under evaluation.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, and preceding restriction/change-of-rings definitions; explicit transpose formulas

proof.text: Apply $E_R$ and $C_R$ to every degree and differential of a cochain complex as defined in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The equation $d^{i+1}d^i=0$ and the chain-map equations become exactly the same equations at $*$. The natural isomorphisms of step 1 applied degreewise are chain isomorphisms and give inverse equivalences of complex categories. A cochain homotopy is a family $h^i:K^i\to L^{i-1}$ with $f^i-g^i=d_L^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_K^i$. The two functors carry this equation to the identical equation and back. Hence they give well-defined inverse functors on maps modulo homotopy, proving the homotopy-category comparison as well.

source.place: Paragraph defining cochain homotopy before Lemma 0112; derived.tex Tag 05RN, section-homotopy

proof.text: For every complex $K$, step 2 identifies the kernels, images and quotients in $H^i(K)=\ker d^i/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$ with the corresponding ordinary-module objects. These identifications commute with chain maps, since the maps on kernels and quotients are induced by their components. Thus $E_RH^i(K)\cong H^i(E_RK)$, and conversely with $C_R$. In the terminology of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], both functors preserve and reflect acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category, and homology.tex Tag 0115, definition-quasi-isomorphism-cochain; explicit cohomology calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact additive functors $E_R,C_R$ of step 2. It gives functors $D(E_R),D(C_R)$ and their natural factorization isomorphisms with the localization functors $Q$. They are inverse equivalences: after precomposition with $Q$, each composite is naturally the identity by the degreewise isomorphisms of step 5. The universal property of localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] descends those natural isomorphisms; their inverses and identities descend too, so their composites remain identities. This proves the derived equivalence and its commutation with localization. The construction applies to unbounded complexes, since the cited factorization lemma is stated for $D(\mathcal A)$, not only $D^+(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category, localization universal property

proof.text: By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], total tensor in degree $n$ is $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}K^p\otimes L^q$ and has differential $d_K\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_L$ on the $(p,q)$ summand. Steps 2 and 3 identify every summand, the direct sum, and both differential components with their module versions. Therefore evaluation identifies the two total tensor complexes by the identity on each pure tensor in each summand. For any acyclic module complex $A$, $C_R(A)$ is acyclic by step 6; applying the K-flat test [def-pc-kflat-complex] and this total-tensor identity proves that evaluation carries a K-flat sheaf complex to a K-flat module complex. Conversely every acyclic sheaf complex is $C_R(A)$ for its acyclic evaluation, so the same test proves the reverse implication. Also flat terms correspond: by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], flatness means exactness of tensoring, and steps 2 and 3 identify the two exactness tests.

source.place: Tag 06YN, definition-K-flat; homology.tex Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex; sites-modules.tex Tag 03ER, definition-flat

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By steps 6 and 8, its evaluation is an ordinary-module K-flat resolution with flat terms, and conversely an ordinary-module resolution gives one by $C_R$. The computation isomorphism of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] represents sheaf derived extension by $Q(P\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S)$. Steps 3--4 identify its chain representative with $E_R(P)\otimes_RS$, and step 7 identifies its localization with the ordinary-module localization. A chain map between K-flat representatives is carried to the same tensor map on both sides. The quasi-isomorphism invariance and canonical comparison for different K-flat resolutions in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] therefore give the same derived computation independently of the resolution. Here the ring map is arbitrary; exactness of extension of scalars is not assumed.

Finally apply [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] to this small singleton site and $\underline\varphi$. Its normalized unit at $QP$, for the flat-term K-flat resolution just chosen, is represented by $P\to\operatorname{Res}(P\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S)$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Step 4 identifies this chain map, including every degree, with the ordinary unit. The same cited statement identifies the transpose of a chain map $g$ by $x\otimes s\mapsto s g(x)$, which evaluation also leaves unchanged. For $q:QP\xrightarrow{\sim}QK$, naturality gives $\eta_{QK}=\operatorname{Res}(L\varphi^*(q))\circ\eta_{QP}\circ q^{-1}$. Evaluation preserves each factor by steps 4, 7 and 9. Hence the comparison of derived computations preserves the unit also at $QK$, as well as on K-flat representatives, proving the final assertion.
